meta.subtitle: Structural wireframe. No behaviour, no styling decisions, no copy that survives.

nav_groups.label: Catalogue
nav_groups.hint: What has been made, and what is missing

nav_groups.label: Provenance
nav_groups.hint: What can be proved about a file

row.summary: Horizontal split. `weights` are flex ratios, one per child.

grid.summary: Uniform grid. `min` is the column floor before wrapping.

region.summary: A labelled area of a screen. The primary structural unit.

card.summary: A bounded panel inside a region.

table.summary: Tabular readout of an entity. Columns come from the binding.

form.summary: Entry surface for an entity. Inputs come from the binding.

detail.summary: Read-only key/value readout of one record.

repeat.summary: A structure that repeats per record. `count` is a placeholder quantity, not data.

gallery.summary: Media tiles. `ratio` is the tile aspect, e.g. 9:16 for vertical.

stats.summary: Metric tiles. Each item names where its number comes from.

actions.summary: Controls. Labels only — this wireframe carries no behaviour.

banner.summary: System notice. `tone` carries state, not decoration.

empty.summary: The state before there is anything. Specified, not left to chance.

text.summary: Placeholder prose. `lines` sets the block height.

media.summary: A single media frame — player, waveform, or still.

slot.summary: A named extension point. Marks where a screen is deliberately unfinished.

screens.title: Roster
screens.purpose: The landing surface. Who is on the roster, and which of them are ready to generate.

children.source: Deployment descriptor — which storage, generator and queue are live
children.note: Always visible. A console running on mock providers must never look identical to one running live.
Summary before detail. Each tile names its own derivation so the number is auditable.

children.title: Roster
children.hint: Sorted by name. Paginated — the collection is not assumed to be small.

children.note: Filtering belongs server-side. Scanning the whole collection to filter in the client is the failure this screen must not repeat.
Identity, consent and songs are separate steps. Registration stays short so it is never the thing that blocks onboarding.

screens.title: Artist
screens.purpose: One roster member: their rights, their stored identity, their catalogue, and what has been generated for them.

children.title: Likeness consent
children.hint: Gates generation. Withdrawal takes effect on the next kit, never retroactively.

children.source: Blocked state — no recorded consent, so kits cannot be generated
children.note: The refusal is a product feature and needs a surface the label can read and act on, not a validation toast.

children.title: Identity
children.hint: The stored description of how this artist reads on screen. Reused by every kit.

children.caption: Reference frames, one per lighting setup

children.title: Songs
children.hint: Each measured once. The measurement is reused by every kit built from it.

children.title: Kits
children.hint: Generated packs, newest first.

screens.title: Identity builder
screens.purpose: Build the artist's reusable on-screen identity once. Editing mints a version; adding evidence does not.

children.source: Version notice — kits already generated stay bound to the version that produced them
children.note: Losing the description a run was generated against makes that run unreproducible.

children.title: Description
children.hint: Text the generator receives before every shot prompt.

children.title: Composed prompt
children.hint: What a provider will actually receive, assembled from the fields on the left.

children.source: Contradiction check between the identity fragment and the shot prompt
children.note: A prompt that describes a face and then asks for an empty centre frame resolves as one or the other. Surfacing the assembled string is how that gets caught before it is bought.

children.title: Reference frames
children.hint: The image half of the identity. One frame per lighting setup, plus accepted stills.

children.caption: Reference frame — lighting setup, framing, content hash
children.note: The domain model carries these and nothing can currently create one. This is the surface that closes that gap.

children.message: No reference frames. The identity is text-only until frames are added.

screens.title: Song
screens.purpose: One measured master. Measurement and hook window are set here once and reused by every kit.

children.title: Master
children.hint: Owned masters only. Uploaded browser-to-bucket; the file never passes through the application.

children.title: Measurement
children.hint: A tempo without a method is refused. The provenance of the number is part of the number.

children.source: Unmeasured state — this song cannot produce a hook-aligned kit yet
children.note: Catalogue onboarding, not compute, is the throughput limit. This screen is where that cost is actually paid, so it should show progress rather than hide it.

children.title: Hook window
children.hint: The one free lever. Drives loop length and travels into every manifest.

children.caption: Selectable hook region against the beat grid

children.message: Nothing generated from this song yet.

screens.title: Kit
screens.purpose: One generated pack: what it cost, what it produced, whether its provenance holds, and whether a human has cleared it.

children.note: The brief the run was built from — shot count, identity version, requested modalities.

children.title: Review
children.hint: A label does not auto-publish AI content about its own artists.

children.title: Progress
children.hint: Generation is minutes. This surface is polled, not streamed.

children.source: Failure state — error text from the run, shown in full

children.title: Assets
children.hint: Vertical loops and cards. Each downloadable with provenance embedded in the file.

children.caption: Generated asset — provider, model, content hash

children.title: Cost
children.hint: What the run actually cost, per step and in total.

screens.title: Catalogue
screens.purpose: The label's actual daily job: what is missing. Which songs are unmeasured, which have no approved kit, whose consent is stale.

children.source: Scope of the current query — tenant, filters applied, records matched
children.note: These are cross-collection questions. Answering them by scanning every record is what this screen must be built to avoid.

items.label: Songs with no approved kit
items.source: count of Song with no Kit at approval=approved

children.title: Gaps
children.hint: One row per song, with each precondition shown as met or missing.

children.note: State reads as form, not only as text — a missing precondition should be visible without reading the cell.

children.title: Spend
children.hint: What generation has cost across the catalogue, and what remains available.

children.source: Budget threshold — generation refused before enqueue once the cap is reached
children.note: A cap enforced before the job is queued is the only place refusing is free.

screens.title: Generate a kit
screens.purpose: The one screen that spends money. Everything on it exists to make the cost and the preconditions legible before the job is queued.

children.title: Preconditions
children.hint: Each is a hard gate. The screen refuses rather than queueing a job that will fail.

children.label: precondition — consent, identity, measurement, hook window

children.source: Unmet precondition, naming the screen that fixes it

children.label: Shot plan — modality, count, mood spread

children.title: Estimate
children.hint: Shown before the job is queued, not after the bill arrives.

items.label: Reused from cache
items.source: count of shots matching a prior content hash

children.note: Reuse is a first-class line. A shot whose prompt, model and parameters already produced an asset should be shown as free before the run, not discovered afterwards.

children.title: Preview
children.hint: The assembled prompt for each shot, exactly as the provider will receive it.

children.label: identity fragment + shot prompt + negative prompt

children.name: craft-toolchain
children.reason: Where a format-driven shot plan would replace a fixed mood list. Unresolved by design — the decision is upstream of this wireframe.

screens.title: Verifier
screens.purpose: Drop in a file, read back what made it. Nothing is looked up — the answer comes out of the bytes.

children.title: Check a file
children.hint: Accepts a media file with an embedded manifest, or a manifest document on its own.

children.source: Verdict — verified, unverified, or no provenance found

children.label: What the verdict means, in plain terms

children.note: One row per step in the run. This is the disclosure the file carries about itself.

children.title: Absent provenance
children.hint: The common case for a file that did not come from here. It is a finding, not an error.

children.message: No manifest found. This file carries no provenance.

screens.title: Deployment
screens.purpose: What this deployment actually is. A console on mock providers must be impossible to mistake for a live one.

children.title: Backends
children.hint: One row per swappable adapter, showing the selected implementation.

children.source: Active warnings from the deployment descriptor

children.title: Tenant
children.hint: Every record, object key and job payload is partitioned by this.

children.name: authentication
children.reason: No sign-in surface is specified. Until one exists every caller resolves to the same tenant, and this screen should say so rather than imply otherwise.
